original_value: In this paper, we report upon our recent work aimed at improving and adapting machine learning algorithms to automatically classify nanoscience images acquired by the Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM). This is done by coupling supervised and unsupervised learning approaches. We first investigate supervised learning on a ten-category data set of images and compare the performance of the different models in terms of training accuracy. Then, we reduce the dimensionality of the features through autoencoders to perform unsupervised learning on a subset of images in a selected range of scales (from 1 μm to 2 μm). Finally, we compare different clustering methods to uncover intrinsic structures in the images.

result.paraphrase: This paper describes our recent effort to improve and adapt machine learning algorithms for automatically classifying nanoscience images obtained with a Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM). The approach combines supervised and unsupervised learning. First, we examine supervised learning on a ten-category image dataset and compare model performance by training accuracy. Next, we use autoencoders to reduce feature dimensionality and apply unsupervised learning to a subset of images selected within a scale range from 1 μm to 2 μm. Finally, we compare several clustering methods to reveal intrinsic structures in the images.
